name: Pit hair laser removal

lead: Laser removal gives smooth underarms for months without shaving, and some people hope the missing hair also means less odor.

Light is absorbed by dark hair pigment and damages the follicle. A 2006 meta-analysis described on Wikipedia found alexandrite and diode lasers reduced hair by about 50 percent for up to six months. Laser hair removal has been FDA-approved in the US since 1997. The studies reviewed measured hair reduction, not odor.

paras: Done in a clinic over a series of sessions spaced weeks apart, on shaved skin. Hair thins gradually across the series.
Side effects are reported as temporary, and were more frequent with diode lasers than alexandrite or intense pulsed light in one 2006 comparison. Darker skin tones need device and clinic care.

angle.text: Laser hair removal gives lasting smooth underarms, and is discussed in looksmaxxing circles as a way to reduce armpit odor by removing hair. Studies show about 50 percent hair reduction for up to six months; they did not test odor.

lead: Laser hair removal uses light absorbed by dark pigment to damage hair follicles. It has been FDA-approved in the US since 1997 and became widespread from the 1990s.[1] Underarms are one area treated, and in looksmaxxing circles the procedure is discussed as a lasting way to reduce armpit odor by removing the hair.

A 2006 meta-analysis described on Wikipedia found alexandrite and diode lasers reduced hair by about 50 percent for up to six months, with no evidence of benefit from intense pulsed light, Nd:YAG, or ruby lasers.[1] The sources reviewed contain no studies of laser hair removal specifically for body odor.
infobox: About 50% up to six months (alexandrite, diode)[1]
Several, depending on hair amount and type[1]

paras: The laser targets pigment in the hair so that follicles are destroyed. Wikipedia's hair removal article says permanence sometimes follows several sessions and that the number needed depends on the amount and type of hair.[1]

Proponents argue that without hair, bacteria and sweat have less to cling to and odor is reduced for longer than with shaving. Wikipedia's hair removal article says hair can collect odor-causing microorganisms.[1] The body odor article says odor arises from skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat, and it notes that armpit hair helps spread odors; it does not discuss hair removal.[2] A 2012 study cited on the underarm hair page reported that shaved armpits were rated as smelling the same as unshaved ones.[3]
A 2006 comparison reported more side effects with diode lasers than with alexandrite lasers or intense pulsed light, and described them as temporary.[1]

No studies found on laser hair removal for body odor. General efficacy findings for laser hair removal on hair reduction are described above.[1] A clinical trial registered as NCT06140199 involves laser in pilonidal disease, a different condition.[4]

timeline.event: Laser hair removal receives FDA approval in the US.[1]
